component.name: Stet
component.summary: Fast, keyboard-first text and code editor

description.p: Stet is a fast text and code editor, quick to drive from the keyboard, that never loses your work: unsaved and untitled tabs survive quitting and rebooting, with no save prompts.

ul.li: Tabs whose unsaved text comes back after a quit or a reboot
Regex find and replace, Find All, and Find and Replace in Files with a results panel
Line tools, case conversion, comment toggling, and JSON and XML formatting
Quick open, a Ctrl+Tab switcher, back and forward
Split view, and two files compared side by side
Careful handling of encodings and line endings, in files up to 256 MiB
Familiar keyboard shortcuts, your own in keys.toml, and an F1 command palette

description.p: Stet follows the system's light or dark style. On Omarchy it also follows the live theme, and changes with it.

screenshot.caption: A Rust file with a search, in Omarchy's Tokyo Night theme

description.p: Restored tabs follow the highlighting limits in config.toml; the command palette and the language and encoding pickers rank like quick open; Open Recent lists files whose names aren't valid UTF-8; a large clean-up of the code.
Stet is also a Flatpak, from its own repository, for Linux systems other than Omarchy and Arch.
A tab dropped after the last tab stays in that strip.
The + follows the tabs, submenus open when you point at them, and Check for Updates… says whether a newer version is out.
A + button opens a new tab.
